subject: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechx.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps

Hi Jane / Alex 

Great to meet earlier this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap:
- Primary use: real-time chat + summarization for customer support agents, plus embeddings for search/rerank.
- Initial expected volume: ~50M tokens/month (phase 1), target ramp to ~500M tokens/mo within 912 months.
- Primary constraint: need to keep inference OPEX within budget while preserving latency for agent workflows.

Open questions we agreed to follow up on (please confirm):
1) Exact expected token mix by feature (chat vs embeddings vs rerank)  ballpark % is fine.
2) Budget range you have in mind for inference (monthly).
3) Target $/1M tokens you consider acceptable for production (we noted a stretch target; want to capture your range).
4) Any CAC / payback targets we should use when modeling ROI for deploying the feature (e.g., 612 months).

Next steps from our side: Ill put together a short unit-economics model showing inference cost at your 50M / 500M scenarios, margin impact per feature, and levers (batching, quantization, model routing, reserved capacity) to get to target $/1M tokens. Ill share the model and propose a 3045 minute follow-up to walk through.

Ive attached a proposed outline and a blank unit-econ model (unit-econ-model.xlsx) for the meeting  please feel free to add numbers or send a copy back.

Thanks  looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa  great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token mix (approx): chat/agent assist ~60%, embeddings (search) ~30%, rerank/batch ops ~10%.
- Volume: for Phase 1 we expect ~50M tokens/month (pilot with ~1k agents), ramp plan takes us to ~500M tokens/month over ~912 months if pilot converts.
- Budget: GVW budget range for inference initially is $15k$30k/month; if economics look strong we can expand in later phases.
- Target $/1M tokens: internal target is ~ $200 / 1M tokens (stated as preferred upper bound for inference cost in production).
- CAC payback target: product/finance prefer 69 months for new paid features (soft).

Ive attached the RFP we circulated internally (FintechX_RFP_Q3.pdf)  Alex is the procurement lead and will join the next call for procurement/redlines.

Thanks  we’re available Mon/Tue next week for a walkthrough.

Jane

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintechx.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechx.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps

Jane  thanks, that is exactly the detail we needed. Quick top-line math so we have a shared baseline before the call: 

Baseline math (using your numbers):
- Phase 1 (50M tokens/mo) at target $200 / 1M tokens => inference OPEX ≈ $10,000 / month.
- Ramp (500M tokens/mo) at $200 / 1M tokens => inference OPEX ≈ $100,000 / month.

What this implies for unit economics and margin (high-level):
- If the feature drives $X revenue per active user (we’ll model several $/feature scenarios), inference should generally be <= 812% of gross revenue attributable to that feature to hit typical margin targets for this product line.
- CAC payback: at 69 months target, we’ll model allowable CAC per net new customer given your expected ARPU uplift from the feature.

Levers we can apply from Redwood to get from $200 down to target economics youd prefer:
1) Quantization + memory-optimized kernels: can reduce $/1M by ~2030% depending on model and quality tolerance.
2) Model routing: put low-latency prompts on a smaller faster/cheaper variant and fall back for complex prompts  can save 1025% depending on mix.
3) Prefix/KV caching for agent workflows (high ROI for small repeated prompts).
4) Reserved capacity / Dedicated pricing: with a 12-month commit we can provide steeper $/1M pricing at higher volumes  I’ll show a few commit tiers.

I attached a quick unit-econ model (unit-econ-model.xlsx) with scenarios: conservative/mid/optimistic for revenue per feature and corresponding margin and CAC payback. If you can drop in your ARPU uplift estimates or sample customer counts we’ll tailor it to FintechX.

Proposed next step: 45-minute walkthrough early next week — I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: model review, pricing levers, procurement checkpoints.

Regards,
Marissa

Attachment: unit-econ-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FintechX baseline & pricing ask

Rishi / Aditya  quick internal note after Jane’s response:

- Their baseline 50M -> 500M ramp and $200 / 1M target gives us clear pressure to propose a competitive committed pricing path. At 50M the spend (~$10k/mo) is modest; the real upside is the ramp to 500M where we can lock in Dedicated economics.
- Proposed playbook for the call: show three pricing scenarios:
  * Self-serve / Hosted: list $/1M = $250 (no commit)  emphasizes time-to-value.
  * 12-mo commit / Dedicated (mid): target $/1M = $140 with X throughput SLA and burst options.
  * 24-mo strategic commit: target $/1M = $100  enterprise packaging + priority routing.
- Highlight operational levers (batching, caching) that can materially reduce observed tokens per user.
- Ask engineering for a quick feasibility check on 1020% additional quantization gains for their model class  if we can claim $/1M reductions from that it strengthens the mid-tier offer.

Can you both review the attached draft pricing grid (redwood-proposal-template.pdf) and the unit-econ model? Ill incorporate and send the external invite.

Thanks  Marissa
